clue.text: Without being foreign, people held to be enemies of Christians

indicators.note: held means the first piece grips the second piece inside it

parts.note: sans is the French word for without, so the foreign version of the word
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a group regarded as hostile to Christians is not in fact foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without being foreign' reads as 'not foreign' but means a foreign word for without; 'held' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens were the Muslim Arabs whom medieval Christendom fought in the Crusades.

clue.text: Note small house in London area

parts.note: so (or sol) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A message left at a small house somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district of London's West End known for nightlife and media firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a well-known district in central London, an example of an area of the capital.

clue.text: Fairy cycling round green? No!

indicators.note: cycling round says the letters of the word rotate, the front pair going round to the back

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian mythology

explanation.surface: A fairy on a bicycle is asked whether she is green and denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling round' moves PE from the front of PERI to the back, giving RIPE. Fruit that is not green is mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is no longer unripe and green is mature and ready to eat, the opposite sense the definition points at.

clue.text: Material is hard substance in which soft mineral is embedded

indicators.note: is embedded means the following pieces sit inside the hard substance

parts.note: coral is the hard stony substance built up by marine polyps
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A geological description of a soft mineral lodged in a hard matrix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is embedded' is the container signal and 'in which' a link; 'Material' is the adjective meaning bodily, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal and material both mean having physical substance rather than being spiritual.

clue.text: A simpleton, being misguided, keeps on offering a particular philosophy

indicators.note: keeps means the anagram holds the following word inside it
misguided suggests the letters have gone astray and must be rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters as printed, though one letter is wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool, led astray, keeps preaching one school of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being misguided' should shuffle A SIMPLETON, but the answer needs a T where that word has an M: a setter's slip. The shuffled letters, with 'keeps' holding ON inside, give the philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoplatonism is the school of thought founded by Plotinus, and its follower or adjective names that particular philosophy.

clue.text: Prophetic male, old buffoon

parts.note: antic is an archaic word for a grotesque clown or buffoon

explanation.surface: A soothsaying man who is also an old clown.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTIC as a noun for a clown is an old usage, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantic is a learned adjective for anything relating to divination or prophecy.

clue.text: A bundle of notes Rex accepted as prize

indicators.note: accepted means the bundle takes the king's letter inside it

parts.note: a wad is a roll or bundle of banknotes
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king receives a thick roll of banknotes as his prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts R inside WAD to make WARD, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: With time, increases delays

parts.note: tempo is musical time or pace
rises means goes up or increases

explanation.surface: Something that grows larger as time passes, holding things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or play for time, so delays is a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Coming together in religious house around work unit

indicators.note: around means the house goes round the unit

parts.note: a convent is a house for a religious community
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Nuns gather in their convent around some task.
explanation.definitionFit: Convergent describes lines or ideas meeting at a point, i.e. coming together.

clue.text: Small particle containing iodine found in Saturn's moon

indicators.note: containing means the particle holds the element's symbol inside it

parts.note: a hyperon is a subatomic particle heavier than a proton
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A scientist detects iodine in a tiny particle on one of Saturn's moons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts I inside HYPERON; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperion is one of the moons of Saturn, named after a Titan.

clue.text: Bloke at counter to prohibit member coming in

indicators.note: coming in means the limb enters the ban

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A man at the bar is barred when a club member walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' is the container signal; 'member' is a limb, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman is the man who serves behind the counter of a pub.

clue.text: Big artist admitting offensive misdeed as entertainer

indicators.note: admitting means the first word lets the next pieces inside

parts.note: fat means big or large
rank means foul-smelling or offensive
a sin is a wrongful act
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A large painter confesses to an outrageous wrongdoing while performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' is the container signal, its contents going into 'Big' only. 'offensive' looks like a noun for an attack but is the adjective meaning foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American singer and actor, an example of an entertainer.

clue.text: Bird seized right off port

parts.note: collared means caught or seized

indicators.note: off says the letter is removed from the port

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A bird is caught by the right as it flies away from a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes R from DOVER (the English Channel port) to leave DOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The collared dove is a common grey-buff dove with a black neck ring, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Going for broke at the casino, man needs good drink

definitions.text: Going for broke at the casino

parts.note: Martin is a man's name
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A gambler at the casino needs a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A martingale is the system of doubling the stake after each loss, which risks everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a betting system of doubling stakes after losses, a way of staking all to recover.

clue.text: Great hand making monarch look embarrassed?

parts.note: royal relates to a monarch
to flush is to go red with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A king or queen blushes red at an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a poker hand: ace, king, queen, jack and ten of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal flush is the strongest hand in poker, the ace-high straight flush.

clue.text: A flowering plant is stemmed

parts.note: a rose is a flowering shrub

explanation.surface: A flower is described as having a stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stemmed' is the verb, as in 'stemmed from', not 'having a stem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose and stemmed both mean came about or originated, as in a problem that stemmed from a mistake.

clue.text: Experiencing vibrations when absorbing a sound

indicators.note: absorbing means the first piece takes the letter in

parts.note: tingling means feeling a prickling or vibrating sensation

explanation.surface: Someone feels a buzzing when they take in a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts A inside TINGLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A ting-a-ling is the tinkling sound of a small bell.

clue.text: Volunteers raised and specially trained may be losing certain rights

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: specially suggests the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers, brought up and drilled, may face losing some privileges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TA (the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve) into AT; 'specially' rearranges TRAINED as TAINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was the old legal forfeiture of civil rights and property after a conviction for treason or felony.

clue.text: Tracks may lead to terminals

indicators.note: the clue suggests rearranging one word may lead to the other set of letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Railway lines that end at stations.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TERMINALS is signalled by 'may lead to'; the surface is about tracks leading to termini.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramlines are the rails on which trams run, a kind of tracks.

clue.text: Link that is given metal coating

indicators.note: coating means the metal goes round the other piece

parts.note: tin is a metal
ie stands for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A connecting part is given a coat of metal plating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' is the container signal and 'given' a link; 'metal coating' reads as one noun phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a connection or link, as with merchandise tied to a film.

clue.text: So he has a zip? Sensible fellow!

definitions.meaning: trousers with no button fly must fasten another way, perhaps with a zip
said of a shrewd person who cannot be fooled

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a man's zipped trousers and praises his good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the flies are the opening of trousers, so lacking them suggests a zip.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a person is alert and hard to deceive, while literally it describes trousers without a fly opening.

clue.text: Classical style for which mocking's not right

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out

parts.note: ironic means mocking or sardonic

explanation.surface: A style of architecture that cannot properly be ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from IRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Country to overthrow religion — but it hasn't succeeded

indicators.note: hasn't means the letter is missing
in a down clue, overthrow means turn the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Islam is a religion

explanation.surface: An attempted coup against a nation's faith fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overthrow' turns ISLAM into MALSI; 'it hasn't' removes S (succeeded, as in genealogies) to leave MALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Sticks up for goody-goody

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a prig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUMS backwards; 'Sticks up for' looks like a phrase meaning defends.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug and goody-goody both describe a self-satisfied, self-righteous manner, used as adjectives.

clue.text: Old girl has rewritten manual

indicators.note: rewritten means the word's letters are set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil has produced a new edition of a handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student; old girl is the British term for a former schoolgirl.

clue.text: Country business where success goes into the book

definitions.text: Country business where success goes into the book

parts.words: Country business where success goes into the book
parts.note: a rural enterprise breeding horses, whose winning bloodlines are recorded in a pedigree register

explanation.surface: A rural firm whose achievements are written up in a register.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'book' is the studbook, the register of thoroughbred pedigrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural establishment for breeding horses, whose successful lines are entered in the studbook.

clue.text: Very old character in charge of society establishing body of principles

parts.note: eth is a letter of the Old English alphabet

explanation.surface: An ancient figure who heads a society sets out its rules.
explanation.walkthrough: ETH (also edh) is a letter used in Old English, hence 'Very old character'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics is the system of moral principles governing conduct.

clue.text: Maintaining railway — attentive about that

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: caring means attentive and considerate

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a railway running and cares about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'that' a link; 'Maintaining' means supporting, as a pillar carries a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying can mean supporting or sustaining, as a beam carries a load, close to maintaining.
